data.name: Crossline
data.detailed_description:
As an ecologist at an Antarctic station, you gain access to a secret complex hidden beneath the ice. Investigate the causes of a fatal disaster and uncover the secrets of a facility that has become an icy grave for its staff.

Immersive Experience

Powered by the Unity engine, the game combines detailed visuals with solid optimization, plunging you into the frozen nightmare of Antarctica. The lack of a HUD and the oppressive atmosphere allow you to fully inhabit the role of an ecologist caught in the heart of a catastrophe.

Linear Narrative

A well-structured story ensures you won’t get lost in the complex's corridors, letting you focus entirely on the details of the disaster. Become part of a gripping tale where every step brings you closer to solving a dark mystery.

Simple Controls

Intuitive controls allow you to focus on survival rather than memorizing keys. In the face of terror, nothing will stand between you and the game's chilling world.

Interactive Environment

The first-person perspective lets you truly touch this world. Many objects are interactive: machinery functions, items react to your actions, and the environment feels alive rather than static. This helps you deeply experience the abandoned complex and its haunting history.

data.short_description: You are an ecologist forced onto a sudden rescue mission inside a secret complex. Face parallel worlds and creatures unknown to science. Piece together the events that led to the tragic disaster and uncover the facility's dark secrets before the cold and madness consume you.

content_descriptors.notes: "The game contains static scenes consistent with a thriller setting within a secret facility. In certain locations, players may encounter the bodies of deceased employees (without detailed mutilation or dismemberment) and visual blood effects on the floor, such as puddles, stains, or trails. This content is purely environmental and narrative-driven, intended to establish the atmosphere of a derelict facility, and does not feature acts of active violence or cruelty toward living beings."
